title: Three 1990s Cartoons That Could Thrive With Modern Reboots
excerpt:
A new feature revisits SWAT Kats, Mighty Max and Bucky O'Hare as reboot candidates.
Only SWAT Kats has a previously announced revival; the other two remain editorial suggestions.
body_md:
The 1990s produced a memorable wave of animated action and adventure series, many closely tied to toy collections. A ComicBook feature argues that three comparatively overlooked shows could find new audiences through contemporary animation. The piece is an editorial wish list, not an announcement that all three projects are in production.

SWAT Kats: The Radical Squadron follows T-Bone and Razor, two feline vigilantes defending Megakat City with advanced aircraft and gadgets. The series also supported an action-figure line. Unlike the other titles on the list, a SWAT Kats revival was announced in 2022, with original creators Christian and Yvon Tremblay involved, although firm release details remain scarce.

Mighty Max began as a miniature playset franchise before becoming a television cartoon in 1993. Its young protagonist uses a magical baseball cap to travel across time and space. The feature suggests that this premise could support an ambitious fantasy reboot, but it does not report an officially commissioned new series.

Bucky O'Hare and the Toad Wars! follows a green rabbit and a team of spacefaring freedom fighters battling the Toad Empire. The original show ran for only 13 episodes but left a strong impression through its inventive science-fiction setting and associated toys.

The argument is ultimately about untapped nostalgic potential. Viewers should distinguish the previously announced SWAT Kats project from the writer's speculative hopes for Mighty Max and Bucky O'Hare.
